description: Report cites evidence from three different sources: a transaction (T1-001), a relationship-graph edge (R1), and a watchlist entity (WATCHLIST1) -- exactly the kind of cross-source grounding the multi-source case architecture (task-007) is meant to support.
report_text: N100 sent funds to M201 (T1-001), an edge confirmed in the relationship graph (R1), and M301 is independently corroborated by a prior watchlist flag (WATCHLIST1).
flag: MAJOR SCOPE FINDING, not a bug to silently fix here: AmlAgent.Evidence.EvidenceScoring.ExtractCitedTxnIds uses the fixed regex \bT[123]-\d{3}\b, which only recognises transaction-id-shaped tokens. The relationship id 'R1' and the watchlist entity id 'WATCHLIST1' in this report are completely invisible to cited_total/cited_distinct/grounded/fabricated_citations -- despite the report genuinely citing them as supporting evidence. Concretely: (1) a report that correctly grounds a claim in relationship/watchlist evidence receives IDENTICAL traceability scores to a report that never mentioned that evidence at all -- there is no positive credit for cross-source grounding; (2) a report that FABRICATES a relationship id (e.g. cites a non-existent 'R99') would likewise never appear in fabricated_citations -- cross-source evidence fabrication currently goes completely undetected by this metric, unlike transaction-id fabrication. This means the current evidence-traceability implementation only actually validates transaction-shaped evidence; its 'evidence traceability' claim does not yet extend to entity/relationship/watchlist/SAR evidence from the canonical multi-source model, even though CanonicalRelationship.EvidenceIds and the case-integrity layer (EvidenceIntegrityValidator) already model and validate exactly that kind of reference at the DATA layer. Closing this gap (extending citation extraction to recognise canonical non-transaction record ids, e.g. relationship/entity/SAR id shapes) is a real, scoped follow-up for evidence-traceability to genuinely cover multi-source cases; it is deliberately not fixed in this validation pass, per the instruction to flag definitional gaps rather than silently patch around them.
